payment_link_line_item_id.description: Stable ID of an existing line item. Omit it to create a new line item.

quantity.description: Whole-number default quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. Omission uses 1. Must be at least 1 for standard links; event tiers also accept 0.

cancel_redirect_url.description: Redirect URL. Send null to clear it.

success_redirect_url.description: Redirect URL. Send null to clear it.

PaymentLinkSalesSummary.description: Paid-order sales totals for a payment link, computed on request. Paid means the order's collection has completed. Fully and partially refunded orders still count, and paid_totals reports the amount collected before refunds. Each order counts once even if it has multiple checkout sessions.

computed_at.description: UTC time at which the summary was computed, at second precision.

paid_order_count.description: Number of orders whose collection has completed, across all currencies, including fully and partially refunded orders.

paid_totals.description: Gross paid totals in integer minor units, one Money object per currency with paid orders, sorted by currency. Refunds are not subtracted. Empty array when there are no paid orders.

refunded_totals.description: Refunded totals in integer minor units on the same paid orders as paid_totals. One Money object per currency with paid orders, sorted by currency, including zero when nothing was refunded. Empty array when there are no paid orders.

PaymentLinkSubscriptionPreview.description: Subscription terms shown before an active plan-backed payment link creates a checkout session.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of billing intervals between recurring charges.

billing_interval_options.description: Billing intervals the plan offers, which the buyer chooses among on the checkout this link opens. The same values as the subscription plan's `billing_interval_options`.

contract_term_months.description: Minimum contract term in months, when configured.

delivery_required.description: True when the plan has a line that ships or is delivered, so each renewal adds a shipping or delivery charge chosen at checkout. The amount is not known until the buyer enters an address and chooses a method.

plan_image.description: Plan image shown to the buyer, when configured.

plan_name.description: Plan name shown to the buyer.

quantity_options.description: Quantities the plan offers, which the buyer chooses among on the checkout this link opens. The same values as the subscription plan's `quantity_options`.

recurring_total_money.description: Recurring total for one billing interval, including line quantities and resolved modifiers.

setup_fee_money.description: Setup fee added to the first amount due, when configured.

trial_period_days.description: Number of trial days before the first recurring charge, when configured.

saved_with.description: Where the buyer saved this payment method. Returned on /v1/me/payment-methods responses when Flint wallet support is enabled. Accept future values.

usage.description: When Flint may charge the payment method. off_session payment methods can pay subscriptions, automatic invoices, and other charges without the buyer, and can be a customer's default. on_session payment methods were saved by the buyer in checkout for faster checkout at this merchant; Flint charges them only in checkouts the buyer completes and refuses them for any charge without the buyer and as a default. Payment methods saved before usage existed are off_session.

payment_option_statuses.description: Availability and validation status of each payment option on this domain.

failure_reason.description: Why a refund failed or a payment refund was canceled. Failed and canceled amounts become refundable again. Fix the cause, then create a new refund with a new idempotency key. Unknown provider values are returned as refund_failed.
x-enum-descriptions: The card can no longer receive credits.
The card was reported lost or stolen.
The refund could not be funded.
Your available balance could not cover the refund.
The card issuer declined the credit.
The refund was stopped at the merchant's request.
The payment is under dispute, or a bank return took the money back first. The buyer already has it through their bank.
On partially_succeeded: one or more payment refunds failed. Read payment_refunds.
This payment refund was canceled before it was attempted because another payment refund failed.
The refund failed with no more specific reason.

status.description: Status of this payment refund or tender allocation. A succeeded refund can still fail after a bank rejection. Follow refund.updated for the parent refund.
x-enum-descriptions: The payment method needs more information before the refund can finish. The parent refund stays pending.
The processor accepted the refund. A bank can still reject it later.
Not attempted because another payment refund in the same refund failed first. failure_reason is payment_refund_not_attempted.

token.description: Opaque processor or browser payment source token.

payment_method_id.description: Saved Flint payment method ID belonging to the customer making this payment.

stripe.description: Stripe credential collected for this payment.

confirmation_token.description: Stripe confirmation token you created with Stripe.js from `payment_collection.stripe`.

type.description: Funding-method family. Wallet payment options use card because their underlying funding source is a card.

PaymentVolumeBucket.description: One full calendar bucket in the response timezone. Payments are selected by creation time (created_at) in the response timezone and counted when their current status is succeeded. All payment amounts and counts use the response currency. Previous values and change_percent are present only with include_previous_period=true and compare the corresponding full calendar bucket in the immediately preceding window. change_percent is omitted when the previous count is zero.

payments_count.description: Succeeded payments created within this bucket. Previous values and change_percent are present only with include_previous_period=true and compare the corresponding full calendar bucket in the immediately preceding window. change_percent is omitted when the previous count is zero.

period_end_at.description: Exclusive bucket end as an RFC 3339 UTC instant.

period_start_at.description: Inclusive bucket start as an RFC 3339 UTC instant.

previous_volume_money.description: Succeeded payment amounts in the corresponding full calendar bucket of the previous window, in the response currency. Present only with include_previous_period=true.

volume_money.description: Succeeded payment amounts for payments created within this bucket, in the response currency.

PaymentVolumeTimeseries.description: Payment volume in full calendar buckets in the response timezone. Payments are selected by creation time (created_at) in the response timezone and counted when their current status is succeeded. All payment amounts and counts use the response currency. Previous values and change_percent are present only with include_previous_period=true and compare the corresponding full calendar bucket in the immediately preceding window. change_percent is omitted when the previous count is zero.

buckets.description: Full calendar buckets selected by payment created_at in the response timezone, including empty buckets.

currencies.description: Every currency with succeeded payments or counted refunds in the current window and, with include_previous_period=true, the previous window, regardless of the currency filter. Empty when neither window contains these payments or refunds.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency selected for every payment amount and count. Defaults to the merchant's default currency when the request omits currency.

has_multiple_currencies.description: Whether currencies contains more than one currency, regardless of the selected currency.

arrival_date.description: Calendar date the bank is expected to receive the funds, in YYYY-MM-DD format using the UTC date of the expected arrival.

balance_source_type.description: Balance source this payout draws from. Flint chooses the source when balance_source_type is omitted at create. Clients must accept source types added in future releases.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

failure_code.description: Flint-normalized payout failure code. Unknown provider values are returned as payout_failed.

failure_message.description: Flint-authored payout failure message. This is stable explanatory text, not a raw provider message.

fee_amount_status.description: Whether the payout fee is estimated or final. not_applicable means no applicable fee status is known, including unmapped fee states.

initiated_by.description: What started the payout. Unmapped sources are returned as other.
x-enum-descriptions: Created through the API or dashboard.
Created by the merchant's payout schedule.
Created by Flint on the merchant's behalf.
An unmapped source started the payout.

method.description: Payout method. instant can appear on imported payouts; unmapped methods are returned as other.

available_payout_methods.description: Payout methods available through Flint for this destination. Only standard is currently available.

disabled_reason.description: Flint-normalized reason the payout destination cannot currently be used. Unknown provider/backend values are returned as destination_unavailable.

status.description: Current status. Archived: deleted, and still readable by ID.
x-enum-descriptions: Archived: deleted, and still readable by ID.

type.description: Destination type. Unmapped destination types are returned as other.

created_at.description: When Flint stored the payout settings record, as an RFC 3339 UTC instant at second precision. Null when no stored settings record exists.

interval.description: Payout schedule interval. Unmapped intervals are returned as other.

updated_at.description: When the stored payout settings record was last updated, as an RFC 3339 UTC instant at second precision. Without a stored record, this is the provider's update time when supplied, otherwise null.

weekly_payout_days.description: Days of the week on which weekly payouts are sent. Allowed values are monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday, saturday, and sunday.

status.description: Whether a bank trace ID is available. Unmapped trace states are returned as unsupported.

PendingPaymentAction.description: Client-side action required before continuing a payment. Resume an order through PayOrder with order_payment_attempt_id, or continue a standalone PaymentIntent through its confirm endpoint without a replacement credential.

action_type.description: Product-level action type. payment_authentication applies to a payment leg; payment_method_authentication applies to saving a future-billing payment method.

client_action.description: Direct browser authority required to finish this action before continuing through Flint. Unlike collection guidance, this payload includes a client secret.

pending_action_id.description: Stable Flint action ID. Use this to deduplicate a repeated action projection while resuming an attempt.

subject.description: The attempt subject that requires browser action. Exactly one of payment_intent or setup_payment_source is present.

PendingPaymentActionSubject.description: Typed subject for a pending order payment action. Exactly one subject is present.

payment_intent.description: PaymentIntent that requires buyer authentication. It can be a standalone intent or an order-owned payment leg.

setup_payment_source.description: Future-billing payment method setup that requires buyer authentication.

PickupFulfillmentDetails.description: Pickup details. For a pickup that checkout creates, location_name, address, and instructions name the store the buyer chose and the delivery method's pickup instructions. The note the buyer left for the store is in recipient.instructions.

address.description: Address where the buyer collects the order.

customer_arrived_at.description: Buyer-reported arrival time for curbside or counter pickup.

expires_at.description: Deadline after which an uncollected pickup should enter merchant review.

instructions.description: Pickup instructions for the buyer, such as where to go on arrival.

location_name.description: Name of the store or place where the buyer collects the order.

pickup_window_duration_seconds.description: Width of the promised pickup window, from 0 to 86400 seconds.

prep_time_duration_seconds.description: Expected preparation time for restaurant and made-to-order pickup, from 0 to 86400 seconds.

vehicle_description.description: Buyer vehicle description used for curbside handoff. Omitted for a checkout session credential that doesn't act for the customer the buyer verified.

city.description: Limited to 255 characters (Unicode code points) on input, counted before surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed and letters are converted to uppercase before validation. The normalized code has 2 ASCII characters; no length limit applies before trimming.

line1.description: Limited to 255 characters (Unicode code points) on input, counted before surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

line2.description: Limited to 255 characters (Unicode code points) on input, counted before surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

postal_code.description: Limited to 32 characters (Unicode code points) on input, counted before surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

state.description: Limited to 255 characters (Unicode code points) on input, counted before surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

charge_money.description: Total of the order's service charges after service-charge discounts.

discount_money.description: Total of order and line-item discounts. Service-charge discounts, such as free shipping, are not included; they reduce charge_money.

requested_tip_money.description: Tip money in the total: the requested tip before payment, and settled tips net of refunds after.

received_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

categories.description: Always present. Empty collections are returned as [].

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

modifier_set_id.description: Attached modifier set. Send null on update to remove it.

variants.description: The variants this request created, ordered by `position` and then `variant_id`. Present only on the `POST /v1/products` response. Read variants later with `GET /v1/products/{product_id}/variants`.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

gift_card_configuration.description: Gift card issuance terms. face_value_money is the reference denomination; unit_price_money is its price. Custom amounts use that price-to-value ratio, rounded to the nearest cent with ties up.

inventory_item_id.description: The inventory item this variant consumes. Present exactly when inventory_tracking is tracked. Several variants may share one inventory item.

modifier_set_id.description: Attached modifier set. Send null on update to remove it.

selected_options.description: Always present. Empty collections are returned as [].

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

gift_card_configuration.description: Only valid for product_type gift_card. Omission creates a fixed denomination at unit_price_money. Discounted pricing requires an explicit face_value_money and price_mode discounted.

images.description: The complete desired gallery in display order. The first image is primary. Send [] to clear the gallery.

metadata.description: Caller-owned metadata. Values can't be empty strings. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API.

modifier_set_id.description: Attached modifier set. Send null on update to remove it.

selected_options.description: Option name and value selections for this variant. When present on an update, replaces the entire selection. Omit to leave unchanged. Select one active value for every active option. null is invalid.

option_name.description: Name of one of the product's options. Limited to 255 characters (Unicode code points) before trimming surrounding whitespace. Matches case-insensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace. On a variant update, an option that is no longer active is accepted only when the entry matches the variant's current selection for that option; omit it to keep that selection.

value.description: Value of the named option. Limited to 255 characters (Unicode code points) before trimming surrounding whitespace. Matches the option's values case-insensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace. A value that is no longer active is accepted only on a variant update, when it matches the variant's current selection for that option.

available.description: Whether the promotion can apply right now: it is active, inside its schedule, under its max_uses, and, when code-gated, has at least one redeemable code.

codes.description: The codes this request created, in request order. Present only on the `POST /v1/promotions` response, where it is `[]` for a promotion created without codes. Read codes later with `GET /v1/promotion-codes?promotion_id=`.

codes_summary.description: Read-only rollup of this promotion's codes. Present only on code-gated promotions; automatic promotions omit it.

display_name.description: Buyer-facing promotion name shown in checkout and order discount surfaces.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

name.description: Internal promotion name for dashboards, searching, and reporting.

stacking_mode.description: continue lets lower-ranked promotions still apply. stop_after admits this promotion and skips every lower-ranked candidate, meaning every candidate with a smaller standalone discount; on a tie, the earlier-created promotion ranks higher.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Set active or inactive with PATCH; DELETE sets archived. An active promotion can still be unavailable: read available.

unavailable_reason.description: Why available is false. Present only when available is false.
x-enum-descriptions: The promotion is set to inactive.
The promotion's schedule.starts_at is in the future.
The promotion has reached its max_uses.
The promotion is code-gated and has no code a buyer can redeem.

PromotionApplicationMethod.description: Canonical REST shape is flat: send type plus the effect fields on this object. Responses always use this flat shape.

allocation.description: How the effect is applied across the matched items or charges. each applies the effect to every matched item independently: a fixed amount_off is charged per item (10 USD off 3 items discounts 30 USD, each capped at the item price), and a percent_off is taken from each item. across applies the effect once to the matched set as a whole: a fixed amount_off is the whole amount one time (10 USD off the group total, not prorated per item), and a percent_off is taken from the combined subtotal. For percent_off the two produce the same total and differ only in how the discount is attributed to individual line items; for amount_off they differ by the number of matched items, so set it deliberately. Defaults to each for line_item and service_charge promotions and across for order promotions. max_discounted_quantity requires each.

applies_to.description: Reserved for future subscription promotion support. Do not send this field in requests.

buy_min_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

calculation_basis.description: Basis for merchandise promotion calculations. Omit for service_charge promotions because service-charge discounts are calculated from the targeted charges.

discounted_item_rules.description: Which line items receive the discount. Required for service_charge promotions, and for line_item promotions whose eligibility_rules include any non-line-item condition (for example order.subtotal or a customer condition). It is optional only when eligibility_rules consist entirely of line_item.* conditions (plus matched_items.subtotal), in which case the matched items are used as the target. Omitting it otherwise returns DISCOUNTED_ITEM_RULES_REQUIRED.

get_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

max_discounted_quantity.description: Maximum number of matched units that receive the discount. Only valid when type is percent_off, and requires allocation each. Sending it with amount_off or buy_x_get_y returns INVALID_MAX_DISCOUNTED_QUANTITY. Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. Flint discounts the first matched units in line-item order (the order items were added), not the cheapest.

recurrence.description: Optional recurrence for subscription payments: once applies to the first charged payment, repeating applies for period_count charged payments, and forever applies to every payment. One-time orders apply the promotion once.

Flint discounts the first matched units in line-item order (the order items were added), not the cheapest.

recurrence.description: Optional recurrence for subscription payments: once applies to the first charged payment, repeating applies for period_count charged payments, and forever applies to every payment. One-time orders apply the promotion once.

PromotionApplicationMethodPatch.description: Send only application_method fields to change. Omitted fields keep their stored values. Sending a different type replaces the effect with the supplied effect fields; allocation, calculation_basis, recurrence, and discounted_item_rules are preserved unless sent, and discounted_item_rules: null clears the stored rules. Money, recurrence, currency_options, and each rule group are replaced whole when present. null clears only nullable fields. discounted_item_rules cannot be null for buy_x_get_y.

allocation.description: How the effect is allocated. Omitted allocation keeps its stored value; it defaults by discount_class only when no allocation is stored. Changing discount_class does not reset allocation.

applies_to.description: Reserved for future subscription promotion support. Do not send this field in requests.

buy_min_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

calculation_basis.description: Basis for merchandise promotion calculations. Omit for service_charge promotions because service-charge discounts are calculated from the targeted charges. Send null to clear it.

discounted_item_rules.description: Which line items receive the discount. Required for service_charge promotions, and for line_item promotions whose eligibility_rules include any non-line-item condition (for example order.subtotal or a customer condition). It is optional only when eligibility_rules consist entirely of line_item.* conditions (plus matched_items.subtotal), in which case the matched items are used as the target. Omitting it otherwise returns DISCOUNTED_ITEM_RULES_REQUIRED.

get_quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

attribute.description: Field the rule tests. The attribute fixes the value type and the operators that are legal for it: money attributes accept comparison operators but not eq or in, booleans accept eq only, and so on. The full attribute/type/operator matrix is machine-readable in x-flint-rule-attributes on this schema. metadata.<key> reads a string from the customer's metadata and accepts the string operators. A disallowed operator is rejected at create time with INVALID_OPERATOR, whose message names the operators allowed for the attribute.

PromotionRuleGroup.description: A rule group is exactly one of three forms, never a blend: an array of rules for a simple list (an implicit AND), an object with only all for nested AND, or an object with only any for OR. The all and any arrays contain rules or nested rule groups. There is no rules key. Sending a rules key, an unexpected key, or both all and any is rejected with INVALID_RULE_GROUP.

PromotionRuleGroupInput.description: A rule group is exactly one of three forms, never a blend: an array of rules for a simple list (an implicit AND), an object with only all for nested AND, or an object with only any for OR. ReturnLineDecision.description: Start from the pinned policy proposal recomputed for approved_quantity when the line has a policy evaluation and the proposal can be built. Otherwise start with return_required_quantity equal to approved_quantity, allowed_resolution_types containing refund, exchange, replacement, and no_monetary_action in that order regardless of whether the original payment is refundable, no automatic_resolution_type, is_inspection_required false, and no receiving_location_id. Each supplied field replaces its starting value; allowed_resolution_types replaces the whole list. Omit automatic_resolution_type to keep its starting value, or send null to resolve manually. Then fill an omitted refund_timing with after_inspection when merchandise is required and inspection is required, after_receipt when merchandise is required without inspection, or after_approval when no merchandise is required. Validate the merged decision for quantity bounds, allowed resolution types, and reachable timing and inspection requirements. A pinned policy always requires override_reason when approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. With a pinned policy but no proposal, other decision fields use these defaults and override_reason is otherwise optional.

allowed_resolution_types.description: Optional replacement for the entire starting list. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal; otherwise refund, exchange, replacement, and no_monetary_action in that order, independent of the original payment's refundability. The resulting list must be valid and non-empty when approved_quantity is above zero.

approved_quantity.description: Required whole-number quantity from zero through the line's requested_quantity; fractional quantities are not supported. When approved_quantity is below requested_quantity, send decline_reason; decline_reason_message is optional. Both decline fields are forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

automatic_resolution_type.description: Optional refund or no_monetary_action that Flint creates and confirms automatically. Omit to keep the policy proposal's value, or the absent value from no-policy defaults. Send null to resolve the line manually; clearing a policy proposal's automatic value requires override_reason. Must be in the resulting allowed_resolution_types. Exchange and replacement cannot be automated. An automatic refund that can no longer run through the original payment's provider fails with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED.

decline_reason_message.description: Optional explanation accompanying decline_reason, up to 2048 characters (Unicode code points), counted before normalization. Requires decline_reason and is forbidden when all requested quantity is approved.

is_inspection_required.description: Optional inspection requirement. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal or false when no proposal can be built. The resulting requirement must be reachable with the merged merchandise quantity and refund timing.

override_reason.description: Required when a decision differs from a buildable pinned policy proposal. With a pinned policy, also required whenever approved_quantity exceeds evaluated eligible_quantity, even when no proposal can be built. The refund timing fill also applies to the proposal and does not count as a deviation. Otherwise optional when a pinned policy proposal cannot be built or no deviation exists. Forbidden without a pinned policy.

override_reason_message.description: Optional explanation accompanying override_reason. Requires override_reason and is forbidden without a pinned policy.

receiving_location_id.description: Optional receiving Location with a postal address. Defaults to the buildable pinned policy proposal or no location when no proposal can be built. Required when the resulting return_required_quantity is above zero and there is no starting location. A process receipt does not supply the decision's location.

refund_timing.description: Optional gate for every resolution type. Defaults to the policy proposal's timing when set. After merging supplied fields, an unset timing becomes after_inspection when return_required_quantity is above zero and inspection is required, after_receipt when return_required_quantity is above zero without inspection, or after_approval when return_required_quantity is zero.

Payment details are attached, but confirmation hasn't finished. Flint usually confirms in the same request that attaches them, so this status is brief unless that confirmation was interrupted. Resume the order's payment attempt, or call confirm with an empty body for a standalone payment intent. No webhook is sent for this status.

The buyer must finish a step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, before the payment can continue. current_payment_action describes the step. Afterward, call confirm with an empty body, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.

A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. cancellation_reason is authorization_expired, and the payment_intent.canceled event reports it.

Read-only shipment state derived from the shipment's package states. An empty shipment remains a created draft.
- `created`: The shipment leg exists but has not been packed or handed off.
- `packed`: The shipment leg is packed and awaiting carrier handoff.
- `shipped`: The shipment leg was handed to the carrier.
- `in_transit`: The carrier is moving the shipment through its network.
- `out_for_delivery`: The shipment is on its final delivery route.
- `delivered`: The carrier reported successful delivery.
- `delivery_attempted`: The carrier attempted delivery but did not complete it. Follow the carrier instructions before retrying delivery.
- `exception`: A carrier exception is blocking normal progress. Resolve the carrier-reported issue.
- `returned`: The shipment was returned toward or to its origin.
- `voided`: The shipment was voided and will not continue through delivery.

x-flint-enum-descriptions.voided: The shipment was voided and will not continue through delivery.

version.description: Monotonic shipment version for expected_version checks.

shipped_at.description: When the shipment was handed to the carrier.

timezone.description: IANA zone the shipping window was entered in, used for display. window_start_at and window_end_at are absolute timestamps, so this does not change the window.

window_end_at.description: End of the scheduled shipping window.

window_start_at.description: Start of the scheduled shipping window.

unit.description: Length unit for length, width, and height. Use millimeter, centimeter, or inch.
Weight unit. Use gram, kilogram, ounce, or pound.

SignedMoney.description: Signed monetary amount represented as integer minor units plus an ISO 4217 currency code.

amount.description: Signed amount in the currency's minor unit, such as cents for USD.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for this amount.

initiated_by.description: Who asked for the skip: buyer, merchant, or integration. Defaults to merchant. Flint's skip email to the buyer says the buyer skipped for buyer, and that the store skipped otherwise.

client_secret.description: Stripe client secret for the named PaymentIntent or SetupIntent.

stripe_js_call.description: Stripe.js operation to perform now. confirm_setup applies to client_setup. Standalone PaymentIntents use payment_collection plus server confirmation instead of initial confirm_payment authority.

StripeClientSetup.description: Stripe.js setup authority returned while saving a payment method. Follow its stripe_js_call now. setup_collection is guidance instead and never carries a secret.

StripeClientSetupStripe.description: Stripe.js initialization context and SetupIntent setup authority.

account_id.description: Stripe connected account ID to pass as stripeAccount when initializing Stripe.js.

publishable_key.description: Stripe publishable key for the active Flint payment mode; use this with account_id when loading Stripe.js.

StripePaymentClientAction.description: Stripe.js initialization context plus one flow-specific authority object. Exactly one of payment_intent or setup_intent is present.

account_id.description: Stripe connected account ID to pass as stripeAccount when initializing Stripe.js.

payment_intent.description: PaymentIntent authority for an order payment authentication action.

publishable_key.description: Stripe publishable key for the active Flint payment mode; use this with account_id when loading Stripe.js.

setup_intent.description: SetupIntent authority for a saved-payment-method authentication action.

client_secret.description: PaymentIntent client secret to pass to Stripe.js handleNextAction.

recurring_amount_money.description: Line amount for the first renewal, including modifiers and recurring discounts, before shipping and tax. Signup-only discounts are excluded.

subscription_offer_id.description: Active subscription offer for this catalog variant.

awaiting_billing_schedule.description: True while an active or trialing subscription on an external billing schedule has no next billing date.

billing_anchor_day.description: UTC day of the month used for monthly and yearly billing. Applies only to Flint-owned schedules.

billing_interval.description: How often the subscription bills, frozen when the subscription was created. Read with billing_interval_count: monthly with a count of 3 bills quarterly.

billing_interval_count.description: Number of billing_interval units between charges, frozen when the subscription was created.

buyer_actions.description: What the buyer can do with the subscription, in this order: cancel, pause, resume, reactivate, update_payment_method, retry_payment, update_delivery, skip, update_billing_interval, update_quantity, swap_items, then renew, under the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. A buyer's read or change through a customer session on /v1/me, or in Flint's buyer account, lists all twelve every time; a merchant read gets an empty list. update_payment_method is required while a payment is past due, due by next_retry_at when a retry is scheduled, and when the card expires before next_billing_at, due by then.

cancel_at_period_end.description: True when the subscription is scheduled to cancel at the end of the current period. Schedule with the cancel route and undo with the reactivate route.

cancellation_details.description: Who asked to cancel, when, and why. Present once a cancellation is requested, whether it takes effect at the end of the billing period or right away. Omitted when no one asked, and removed when a scheduled cancellation is undone. See cancellation_reason for voluntary and payment-related cancellations.

cancellation_reason.description: Why the subscription is canceled or scheduled to cancel. Uses cancellation_details.requested_by when recorded, payment_failed for a canceled subscription without a requester, and other for a scheduled cancellation without a requester. Omitted otherwise.
x-enum-descriptions: Payment failed without a recorded cancellation request.
A cancellation is scheduled without a recorded requester.

delivery.description: Saved delivery preference with the current delivery method display. Write responses use the same display as GET: fixed shipping reflects the current method configuration, and quoted shipping shows the last paid shipping amount when available.

delivery_hold.description: Current delivery issue that blocks collection. Mutually exclusive with upcoming_delivery_hold.

early_termination_fee_money.description: Early termination fee frozen in the subscription's contract terms. Present only before contract_end_at when those terms include a fee. Later plan changes do not change this fee.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

inventory_wait.description: Renewal waiting for stock. Included only in merchant responses and omitted from buyer responses.

missed_billing_at.description: The billing date whose payment failed, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Present only while status is past_due. When it's before current_period_end_at, the first paid period was never paid, so canceling ends the subscription right away whatever cancel_immediately says.

next_billing_at.description: When Flint next starts a scheduled renewal charge, as an RFC3339 timestamp. Present only while a trialing or active subscription has a billing date and isn't set to cancel at the end of its period. Absent when no renewal is scheduled: a paused subscription resumes at scheduled_resume_at, a past_due one reports the failed billing date in missed_billing_at and retries at next_retry_at, an incomplete one retries at next_retry_at, a scheduled start begins at starts_at, one set to cancel ends at current_period_end_at, and an external schedule awaiting a date reports awaiting_billing_schedule.

next_retry_at.description: Recorded automatic payment retry time. Null when no retry time is available.

open_renewal_order_id.description: ID of the paid renewal order whose shipment has not been dispatched. It keeps its committed delivery destination after preference changes and cancellation. Absent when no such renewal order exists. Only renewal orders count; the signup order is not included.

pause_reason.description: Why the subscription is paused: merchant for a pause made with your API key or dashboard, buyer for the buyer's own pause, delivery_action_required for a pause during or after a delivery hold, and payment_failed when renewal payment retries ran out and your dunning settings pause the subscription. Omitted when the subscription is not paused.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

recurring_amount_money.description: What one billing period charges before tax and discounts, frozen when the subscription was created. Plan price changes after that do not change it.

scheduled_resume_at.description: When a pause with a length (pause_duration_cycles) resumes on its own: that many billing intervals after paused_at. Null when the subscription is not paused or the pause has no length, such as a pause until you resume it or the pause Flint starts when a delivery hold runs out.

service_location.description: Omitted for a checkout session credential that doesn't act for the customer the buyer verified.

starts_at.description: When a scheduled start's first billing period begins. Present only until that first payment succeeds.

upcoming_delivery_hold.description: Delivery issue forecast for the next renewal at renewal_at. Mutually exclusive with delivery_hold.

SubscriptionBillingStartInput.description: How billing begins. Send exactly one closed tagged-union branch.

starts_at.description: Future instant when the first billing period starts.

completed_cycles.description: Number of billing cycles already charged on the previous billing system, including the current imported period. The subscription's completed_cycles starts here, and the next renewal's subscription_cycle is this number plus one.

period_started_at.description: Start of the already-running billing period being imported.

SubscriptionCancellationDetails.description: The cancellation request behind a scheduled or completed cancellation.

comment.description: What the requester wrote. Only merchant credentials read it; buyers never receive it. Omitted when none was given, and cleared when the customer is deleted.

reason_code.description: The reason the requester chose. Omitted when none was given.

requested_by.description: buyer: the buyer, in Flint's buyer account or with a customer session. merchant: a merchant credential, such as an API key or the dashboard.

delivery_version.description: Version of the subscription's saved delivery preference.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the delivery preference. Omitted until the preference changes after creation. Pairs with updated_at.

The merchant changed the delivery preference through the API or dashboard.
A delivery migration changed the delivery preference.

address.description: Resolved delivery address used by future shipments.

customer_address_id.description: Display reference to the saved customer address used when this destination was written. Editing that saved address does not change the subscription destination.

current.description: True when this is the subscription's saved preferred delivery method, including when unavailable.

failure_category.description: Reason the method cannot serve this subscription destination. Values can expand as delivery capabilities change.

selectable.description: True when this method is offered, renewable, and currently serves the destination.

unavailable_reason.description: Reason the method cannot serve this subscription destination. Values can expand as delivery capabilities change.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

product_ids.description: Catalog targets for new signups. At least one product or variant is required.

promotion_id.description: An active promotion with forever recurrence. On PATCH, null removes the discount for new signups; omission keeps it.

subscription_delivery_method_ids.description: Delivery methods offered at signup. An empty array uses the store's checkout defaults. Existing subscriptions keep their selected method.

variant_ids.description: Catalog targets for new signups. At least one product or variant is required.

external_reference_id.description: Caller-owned identifier for this resource in an external system.

inventory_routing_source.description: Where tracked demand from this plan is routed. New subscriptions and payment links for the plan copy it. Absent when the plan has no source.

status.description: Active plans accept new signups. Inactive plans refuse new signups with PLAN_NOT_ACTIVE while existing subscriptions keep renewing. Archived plans are read-only and their status is set only by DELETE /v1/subscription-plans/{subscription_plan_id}.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

swap_variants.description: Current sellable alternatives in swap_variant_ids order, excluding the line's own variant and variants priced in a different currency. Present on variant lines, including an empty array.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

delivery_methods.description: Present in delivery_options mode ([] when no method applies); absent in create mode.

errors.description: Present in create mode ([] when the subscription is valid); absent in delivery_options mode.

is_valid.description: Present in create mode; absent in delivery_options mode.

renewal_at.description: Time of the next renewal affected by this delivery issue.

Send an object to merge by key, set a key to null to remove it, or set metadata to null to clear all caller-owned metadata. An empty object makes no change. Values can't be empty strings. Keys starting with flint_ are reserved for Flint, are not returned, and cannot be written through the public API.

quantity.description: Whole-number quantity; fractional quantities are not supported.

api_version.description: Set default to follow the merchant default, or a supported YYYY-MM-DD version to pin this endpoint. Omit to leave unchanged. Null is not accepted. Switching between a pin and default clears the rollback offer.

description.description: Endpoint description. Omit to leave unchanged; null clears it. Send null to clear it.

enabled_events.description: Event types to deliver. Send ["*"] for every type the endpoint's event_sources deliver, including types added later; * must be the only entry and is not available with installed_merchants. At least one entry is required. Previous event type names from the 2026-10 rename are accepted for one release and are stored and returned under their new names. See the [changelog](/docs/changelog).

event_sources.description: Event sources this endpoint receives. Defaults to merchant. Use partner_app for app lifecycle events and installed_merchants for events from merchants that installed the partner app.

expected_api_version.description: Apply api_version only if this matches the resource's current api_version. A mismatch returns HTTP 409. Requires api_version; null is not accepted.

installed_merchant_modes.description: Modes of installed-merchant events this endpoint receives. Required when event_sources includes installed_merchants and omitted otherwise. Partner app lifecycle events are delivered regardless of these modes.

partner_app_id.description: Partner app that owns partner_app or installed_merchants event sources.

x-enum-descriptions: Receives no events; pending deliveries were suppressed.

expected_version.description: Optional version of the parent Return. A stale value returns RETURN_VERSION_CONFLICT with the current Return version.

buyer_notification_behavior.description: Controls buyer email handling. Omit or use send to send when recipient, template, and deduplication rules allow it. Use suppress when another system owns buyer messaging.

expected_version.description: Optional resource version last read by the caller.

WebhookEndpoint.description: A merchant webhook endpoint belongs to the live mode or sandbox of the credential that created it and receives only that environment's events. Partner endpoints select sources with event_sources and installed_merchant_modes.

api_version.description: A dated API version pins this endpoint. The value default follows the endpoint owner's merchant default at delivery time, including retries. Deliveries never use a newer version than the event's recorded version.

api_version_previous.description: Version this endpoint used before its last upgrade. Present while a rollback is available. To roll back, send it as api_version.

api_version_rollback_expires_at.description: When the rollback offer for api_version_previous ends. You can still set any supported version afterward.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: When the replaced signing secret stops signing deliveries. Present only during a rotation overlap. Until then each delivery carries a signature from both secrets.

ApiKeyHeader.description: Flint secret API key sent directly in the X-API-Key header. Secret keys use the flint_live_ or flint_test_ prefix; keep ordinary secret keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception.
ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key

BearerAuth.bearerFormat: Flint API key, partner install token, or short-lived Flint session token
BearerAuth.description: Flint secret API key, CLI OAuth access token, installation-scoped partner token, or session token sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Route-specific partner access and scopes are declared by x-flint-partner-access and x-flint-partner-required-scopes. Secret API keys use the flint_live_ or flint_test_ prefix; keep ordinary secret keys server-side.

CustomerSessionBearer.description: Short-lived, server-side customer session secret. Accepted only by /v1/me endpoints.

InvoiceAccessTokenBearer.description: Invoice access token from the invoice's public URL. Accepted only for that invoice's buyer detail, PDF, and checkout-session endpoints.

OnboardingSessionBearer.description: Short-lived onboarding token returned by POST /v1/onboarding/verify-email. Onboarding and merchant account sessions are limited to the merchant's default sandbox unless sandbox_id names another sandbox of the same merchant. Refresh stays bound to the launch token's sandbox. Live onboarding requires a live API key created in the dashboard.

info.description: Flint's public /v1 API for payments, checkout, invoices, subscriptions, catalog, customers, returns, inventory, money movement, webhooks, and developer operations. Use live keys for production and sandbox-bound test keys for staging or sandbox workflows; keep ordinary secret API keys server-side. The first-party docs playground uses a dedicated sandbox-only sample key exception. A request body can be up to 1 MiB unless an operation documents a lower limit; a larger body returns 413 with the REQUEST_BODY_TOO_LARGE error code.

patch.description: Updates the mutable fields of a checkout session. A merchant credential can update metadata and external_reference_id, including after the session ends. Send external_reference_id as null to clear it, or metadata as null to clear all metadata. On a session with a subscription_plan_id, either credential can send subscription_terms with the buyer's billing interval and quantity while the session is open and no payment is in progress; a change reprices the signup order and releases the delivery selection. The session's own checkout credential can also send buyer_contact and timezone while the session is open. The buyer_contact field saves the email and phone the buyer entered; send a contact field as null to clear it. The timezone field records the buyer's IANA time zone, which Flint uses for times in the emails it sends the buyer. Saving the same values again changes nothing.

post.description: Sends the buyer a six-digit code that confirms they control an email address or a mobile phone number, so the checkout can save their card or use the details they saved at this merchant before. Only the session's own checkout credential can call it, and no payment attempt may be in progress. With channel email, Flint emails the code, while the session is open and save_payment_method_requires_verification is true. With purpose save_payment_method, whose default channel is email, Flint sends a code to any valid address. With purpose use_saved_payment_methods and channel email, Flint sends one only when a customer with that email has saved details, cards saved by email or with a mobile phone number, and the response is the same either way, so it never reveals whether the email shops at the merchant. The emailed code opens only the cards saved by email; confirming it when there are none still binds the checkout to the customer, so the buyer can save a card with their own number, which replaces the customer's saved number. With channel sms and purpose use_saved_payment_methods, Flint texts the code to the mobile phone number saved with that email's details at the merchant, and returns channel sms and phone_last_digits. Always offer the emailed code beside it. When the email has no details saved with a number, or Flint cannot text now, it texts nothing and returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_TEXT_UNAVAILABLE; offer the emailed code instead. This answer tells anyone who types the email whether it has details saved with a number at the merchant, and the number's last two digits. A texted code opens only the cards saved with that number, and an emailed code opens only the cards saved by email. Every text reads "Your Flint Pay verification code is: " and the code, and names Flint Pay rather than the merchant, so the prompt for the code should say it comes from Flint Pay. A new text to a number ends the code any other checkout, at any merchant, texted to it, so only the latest texted code for a number works. With purpose use_saved_payment_methods and channel auto, its default, a checkout asks as the buyer leaves the email field, and Flint sends the code the way the email's details were saved: it texts the mobile phone number they carry, as channel sms does, or, when they carry none, emails a code when the email has cards saved by email. The response's channel says which. For an email with neither, or past a cap, it sends nothing and returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_NOT_SENT; show nothing about saved details then. So this answer tells anyone who types the email whether it has saved details at the merchant; name channel email for an answer that doesn't. While an emailed code a checkout sent this way still works, another auto request for the same email answers with that code and sends nothing; request channel email to send another. With purpose confirm_saved_payment_method, after a payment that sent save_payment_method_phone, Flint sends the code that confirms the saved card: channel sms texts the number given with the payment, and channel email emails the customer's email, only when it is the email the payment was made with; otherwise it refuses the request with a 409, and the texted code confirms the card. The response shows that email masked, such as a•••@example.com. Send no email with it. It works on the paid session, or the open one whose payment is approved for the merchant to capture later, until payment_method_save.status leaves pending. A texted code saves the card with the number when the payment created the customer, when the buyer confirmed the customer's email in this checkout, or when the number is already the customer's saved number and a card saved with it is active. Otherwise payment_method_save.email_confirmation_required becomes true, and an emailed code finishes the save. A card saved with a number makes it the customer's saved number: the cards saved with the number it replaces are removed, with payment_method.removed. An emailed code works for 15 minutes and a texted code for 10, each for 5 tries, and a new request replaces the checkout's earlier codes. A checkout can request 5 emailed codes and 6 text lookups with 3 texts before paying, and 3 of each channel to confirm a saved card; codes can be requested for one email 3 times in 15 minutes and 10 times in 24 hours at the merchant; one number gets 3 texts in 10 minutes and 10 in 24 hours; one network can have 10 texts sent and 10 codes emailed by channel auto, and make 30 text and auto requests together, an hour, and 20 requests of any kind a minute. When you call Flint with the checkout credential from your own server, these network caps count per merchant environment and calling IP address, and are ten times higher. A text request over a cap on texts, the checkout's, the network's, or the number's, returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_TEXT_UNAVAILABLE, like an email with no number to text; over a cap on text requests, it returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_LIMIT_REACHED for the checkout and RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, without param email, for the network. A merchant's checkouts can send 1,000 texts in 24 hours; past that, text requests return CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_TEXT_UNAVAILABLE. After 10 wrong tries in 24 hours, or 30 in 7 days, across the codes for one email at the merchant or texted to one number, Flint sends that email or number no codes and accepts none of its codes. In a sandbox, Flint sends no texts: a texted code's request answers as if it texted the number, and to confirm it, 000000 is a wrong code, 999999 returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE, and any other six digits confirm it. Emailed codes arrive as in live mode. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same code request and sends no second email or text.

post.description: Checks the code the buyer typed. A right code makes the checkout act for the customer with that email, and creates the customer, with a customer.created event, when none exists. The checkout can then save the buyer's card with save_payment_method on POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay, and list and pay with that customer's saved cards. The order's customer does not change until the payment succeeds. Only the checkout_auth_token in the response acts for that customer. Send it as X-Checkout-Session-Secret from then on. Every other credential for the session, including earlier checkout_auth_token values and hosted checkout links, keeps working for the checkout and acts for no customer, so it lists no saved cards and pays with none. A buyer who opens the link on another device confirms an email there to use them, and from then on only that device's new credential acts for a customer. If the response is lost after the code was accepted, the credential you sent still works. Send the same code again with it while the code is valid, which counts as another try and returns a new credential for the same customer, or request a new code. A wrong, expired, or replaced code returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_CODE_INVALID, and so does a used code once the checkout was confirmed again, any code after its 5th try, any code for an email past its limit on wrong tries, or a code whose email's customer changed its email or was deleted after the code was sent. If the checkout stops offering saved payment details before the code is confirmed, such as when the merchant turns them off, the request returns CUSTOMER_VERIFICATION_NOT_OFFERED. A credential that already acts for a customer gets CHECKOUT_CUSTOMER_ALREADY_AUTHORIZED, and confirming never replaces a customer the merchant named. Once the customer whose email the buyer confirmed changes that email or is deleted, the checkout acts for no customer, and the buyer can confirm the customer's new email or another one. A checkout opened from a checkout reminder link acts for no customer the buyer confirmed earlier, so its buyer confirms an email again. A texted code for saved details binds the checkout the same way, but the new credential opens only the cards saved with that number: it lists and pays with no card saved by email, and reads no customer details. A texted code checks once, so after a lost answer request a new code. A code for purpose confirm_saved_payment_method keeps the session's credential, so the response has no checkout_access, and its checkout_session carries payment_method_save. A texted code saves the card with the number when the number already opens the customer's saved details or the customer has none yet; otherwise payment_method_save.email_confirmation_required turns true, and an emailed code finishes the save. An emailed code alone saves the card by email. After success, a retry with the same Idempotency-Key and code returns the stored answer and credential to any credential of the session. After failure, a retry checks the code again and counts as another try.

post.description: Applies credit from an issued credit note to its invoice, reducing outstanding_money. The amount cannot exceed the credit note's unallocated_money or the invoice's outstanding balance. Closing the balance with credit sets the invoice to credited. post.description: Issues a draft credit note and freezes its PDF. Optionally provide refund to initiate a linked refund on a paid invoice. Idempotency-Key is required with or without refund and is retained for as long as the issue's effects exist, scoped to merchant, environment, credit note, and key. Reuse the key with the identical request to recover the original result. After a lost response with refund, list this note's refunds filtered by idempotency_key. A pending refund is accepted, not completed. Without refund, issuance does not move money. Issue validates the stored preview against current shared creditable pools. A fitting correction whose preview changed returns CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION with reason credit_note_creditable_value_changed: replace its existing corrections with PATCH using the current expected_version, review the recalculated amounts, and issue again. A correction exceeding the remaining pool returns CREDIT_NOTE_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CREDITABLE. Affected historical tax allocations return ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED with reason credit_note_tax_reconciliation_required.

post.description: Signs the buyer in to your Flint-hosted customer account as this customer. Works for 15 minutes and one open. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Requires customers.sessions.write. Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this customer's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its open. Without an Idempotency-Key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with X-Request-Id before sending a new request.

delete.description: Retires the delivery method after checking current dependencies. The retired resource remains available by ID for historical records. Deleting an already archived resource returns it without changing its version or repeating effects. A method referenced by checkout.default_delivery_method_ids at merchant scope or by delivery_method_ids on an active or inactive payment link cannot be archived; the request returns 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE with the blocking references. Remove the method from checkout.default_delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/settings or from the link's delivery_method_ids with PATCH /v1/payment-links/{payment_link_id}. Open checkout sessions keep their pinned revision and do not block retirement.

post.description: Ends the active or provisioning demo session identified by demo_session_id for this client and provisions a fresh one. A client that lost its create response gets the current demo_session_id from the error on ACTIVE_DEMO_SESSION_EXISTS or DEMO_SESSION_SECRET_REPLAY_EXPIRED. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key and body replays the replacement before checking the current session, including its secret during the secret delivery window. After that window, the retry returns DEMO_SESSION_SECRET_REPLAY_EXPIRED. The daily cap applies only to fresh executions. Omit template to use quickstart; an explicit empty or unsupported value is invalid.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of disputes for the authenticated merchant with optional payment, customer, status, reason, case type, action required, and timing filters. Defaults to created_at descending. The amount sort compares amount_money.amount in minor units. The evidence_due_at sort places disputes without deadlines last in either direction.

parameters.name: payment_intent_id

parameters.description: Optional Flint order ID filter.
parameters.name: order_id

parameters.description: Optional Flint customer ID filter.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Optional dispute status filter.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: The issuer asked for information before any chargeback. Respond by evidence_due_at.
You responded to the inquiry and the issuer is reviewing it.
The inquiry closed without becoming a chargeback. Final.
A chargeback is open and needs your response by evidence_due_at.
Evidence was submitted and the bank is deciding.
Decided against you, or a bank return that could not be contested. Final.
Resolved before it became a chargeback. Final.
Flint received a dispute state it does not recognize yet. Not final. Treat the dispute as open, do not assume an outcome, and read it again later. A response session still opens.

parameters.description: Optional normalized dispute reason filter.
parameters.name: reason

x-enum-descriptions: The buyer reported the payment as fraudulent.
The buyer did not recognize the payment.
The buyer reported a duplicate payment.
The buyer did not receive the product or service.
The product or service was not as described.
An expected refund was not processed.
The buyer reported a payment after canceling a subscription.
The payment did not comply with applicable rules.
The bank account had insufficient funds.
The bank account could not be found.
Another reason, including a reason Flint does not recognize yet.

parameters.description: Optional dispute case type filter.
parameters.name: case_type

x-enum-descriptions: A non-card dispute, such as a buy now, pay later claim, or a card case type Flint does not recognize yet.

parameters.description: Filter by whether a merchant response is needed now. True includes needs_response and inquiry_needs_response disputes that allow evidence and whose evidence deadline has not passed; false includes the remaining disputes.
parameters.name: action_required

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by dispute_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on evidence_due_at.
parameters.name: evidence_due_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on evidence_due_at.
parameters.name: evidence_due_before

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.

post.description: Upload a local image to Flint. Create a file, PUT the bytes to upload.url with upload.method and every upload.headers value, then POST /v1/files/{file_id}/complete. The URL works for 15 minutes. Purpose requires its own write scope: product and product_variant use commerce.products.write; bundle uses commerce.bundles.write; payment_link uses checkouts.payment_links.write; subscription_plan uses commerce.subscription_plans.write; merchant_logo and merchant_icon use merchants.profile.write. Logo and icon files are merchant-wide; all other purposes belong to the authenticated environment. Partner installs can upload commerce images but cannot upload merchant_logo or merchant_icon: those purposes return INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE with scope_requirement because merchants.profile.write is not grantable to installs. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, and route. A replay returns the original upload target without extending its expiry. If a result cannot be recovered, contact support with X-Request-Id before starting another upload.

post.description: After PUT succeeds, complete the file to process its image. Returns the ready file; completing a ready file again returns it. Send no request body or {}. Completing before the bytes arrive returns FILE_NOT_UPLOADED and leaves the file awaiting_upload. Attach the returned url as images[].source_url before expires_at, 24 hours after processing. Completion requires the purpose's write scope, with the same merchant-wide branding and environment boundaries as createFile. Partner installs can upload commerce images but cannot upload merchant_logo or merchant_icon: those purposes return INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE with scope_requirement because merchants.profile.write is not grantable to installs. Idempotency is scoped to merchant, credential, environment, route, and file_id. A replay returns the original result; it does not extend upload or attachment deadlines. After a lost completion response, repeat this route with the same key and file_id.

patch.description: Replace a count's complete observation set atomically. expected_version is required when replacing observations. Send every item exactly once with the count's current expected_version and each observation's required expected_physical_version. Read the level before physically counting; zero is valid for a missing level. Every assertion must match locked current stock or the whole save is refused. Preserve saved quantities and fences for unchanged lines. Recount affected items before supplying fresh fences, even when quantities are unchanged. Omitted condition quantities retain the matching level snapshot's values. occurred_at records provenance and does not reconstruct historical stock. Idempotency is scoped to the authenticated merchant, environment, and endpoint. Its fingerprint includes the canonical request body. To recover the command's effects after a lost response, read the relevant resource or inventory movement list.

post.description: Creates an invoice draft from exactly one source: order_id for an order-backed invoice, or quick_pay for an invoice with a new backing order. Include issue to issue it immediately, using merchant_default delivery when issue is empty. Idempotency-Key is required for every request because issuing an automatic-collection invoice can charge the buyer. Replays preserve the original invoice result and recover its current public_url only within 24 hours of the original request; later replays omit public_url. Use GET /v1/invoices/{invoice_id} for the current invoice. If Flint returns IDEMPOTENCY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED, contact Flint support with the original Idempotency-Key and request ID. Never retry with a new key.

post.description: Returns the current open invoice checkout session and aligned card attempt when they still match the invoice balance and collection run. A newly created session and attempt share the fixed expiration of the active invoice public-link generation. Unexpired sessions are reused regardless of remaining lifetime; active payment work returns a resolving conflict instead of creating competing collection. When the invoice's order has items to deliver, a new session offers the delivery methods in settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids, and the request fails with a validation error when those methods cannot deliver every item. return_url sets where the checkout sends the buyer after paying. A reused session takes a new return_url only until a payment starts on it, and keeps the one it has after that.

post.description: Sends short-lived confirmation codes to the current and new email addresses. If the account has no current email, only the new address must be confirmed. The customer email does not change until confirmation succeeds. Limited to three attempts per 15 minutes, including attempts rejected because the email is already used. A rejected attempt keeps any pending email change request. Over the limit, the request returns 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with Retry-After set to the whole seconds until the oldest counted attempt leaves the window, at least 1.

Sign the buyer in again with the new email.

get.summary: List cards saved with Flint for this store

post.description: Records the buyer's consent to save an independent store copy for off-session payments, including subscriptions. Call only after the buyer agrees. Requires a live email-code buyer login and an enabled Flint wallet at a Flint-hosted store account. Supply an id from listMeFlintWalletPaymentMethods. Confirm client_setup with Stripe.js confirmSetup, then poll GET /v1/me/payment-methods/{payment_method_id} until active before changing a subscription through /v1/me/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/payment-method. Setup may request authentication. Removing the platform card or revoking store consent blocks the copy immediately. Idempotency-Key is optional and scoped to the store, customer, card handle, and key. Responses are retained for 24 hours. After a copy is revoked, retries with any key bound to that copy are refused. Get new consent and use a new key to create another copy. Retry a lost response with the same key. Concurrent requests for the same card at this store share one copy and setup. A failed off-session charge can still require the buyer to return through the existing card-update link. Accept an empty body or {}.

get.summary: Get one of the current buyer's invoices

post.description: Accepts a customer session, which limits the request to that customer's invoices, or the access token from this invoice's public link, which limits it to this invoice. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns the current open invoice checkout session and aligned card attempt when they still match the invoice balance and collection run. A newly created session and attempt share the fixed expiration of the active invoice public-link generation. Unexpired sessions are reused regardless of remaining lifetime; active payment work returns a resolving conflict instead of creating competing collection. When the invoice's order has items to deliver, a new session offers the delivery methods in settings.checkout.default_delivery_method_ids, and the request fails with a validation error when those methods cannot deliver every item. return_url sets where the checkout sends the buyer after paying. A reused session takes a new return_url only until a payment starts on it, and keeps the one it has after that.

get.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource.

x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Submit payment details again to retry.
Payment details are attached, but the payment hasn't been confirmed yet. This status is brief unless the confirmation was interrupted.
A step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, must be finished before the payment can continue. current_payment_action describes the step.
Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly.
A hold is in place on the payment method and no money has been collected. The merchant collects some or all of it, or releases it, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected. Final. cancellation_reason says why when it is known. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.
A hold reached authorization_expires_at without being collected, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. cancellation_reason is authorization_expired.

post.summary: Preview Return eligibility or resolution amounts for the current buyer

post.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Create or reuse a hosted or embedded checkout session for the buyer's balance on a replacement order linked to this return resolution. Returns 200 when reusing an existing session and 201 when creating one. Omit surface to use hosted. The same surface reuses the open session; changing surface replaces an idle session and is refused while a payment is in progress. Use redirects to set where the buyer goes after paying or canceling. The return_url field is an alias for redirects.success_redirect_url and must be an address of the merchant's customer account. A reused session takes a new success destination only until a payment starts, then keeps its existing destination.

get.description: Uses the customer identity fixed by the customer session. The request cannot select a customer_id. Lists the buyer's subscriptions. Subscriptions without a next_billing_at never match next_billing_after or next_billing_before, and sort last with sort_by=next_billing_at in either direction. subscription_plan is always included without expand: the plan's current summary, or null when the subscription has no plan.

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous list response.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by subscription status. Repeat the parameter or pass comma-separated values to match multiple statuses.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Filter by the system that supplies billing dates.
parameters.name: billing_schedule_owner

parameters.description: When true, returns subscriptions scheduled to cancel at the end of the current period that are not yet canceled. When false, returns every other subscription.
parameters.name: cancel_at_period_end

parameters.description: Filter by the subscription's selected delivery method.
parameters.name: delivery_method_id

parameters.description: Filter by the reason of the current delivery_hold. Does not match upcoming delivery issues.
parameters.name: hold_reason

parameters.description: Filter by Flint subscription plan ID.
parameters.name: subscription_plan_id

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by subscription_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_before

parameters.description: True matches subscriptions with a delivery hold, an upcoming delivery hold, or a delivery-action-required pause, plus past_due or incomplete subscriptions and active subscriptions whose billing date passed more than 24 hours ago without a renewal. False is the exact complement. Other filters still apply.
