post.description: Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires a full buyer session and Idempotency-Key. Send expected_version to reject concurrent changes. Retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt with status 200, including when the payment is declined. Inspect payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment.

post.description: Creates a fresh provider session from a signed launch token after rechecking the authenticated principal, merchant environment, account controller, and component grant. An onboarding session can refresh only sandbox launch tokens created by the same user with an onboarding session. The sandbox is pinned by the launch token, using the merchant's default sandbox unless sandbox_id named another sandbox of the same merchant at creation. Live onboarding requires a live API key, and refresh requires the same API key that created the launch token. A completed retry with the same Idempotency-Key creates a fresh launch session instead of replaying a prior client secret.

get.description: Starts a partner app install in the merchant's browser. Flint validates the request, then redirects to Flint's consent screen, where the merchant signs in, chooses a merchant, and approves or denies the requested permissions. Flint then redirects to redirect_uri with code, state, and mode, or with an OAuth error. Request errors found before consent also redirect with an OAuth error once client_id and redirect_uri are validated. Unknown or inactive clients and missing or unregistered redirect URIs return the Flint error envelope.

The required scope field contains the full requested set as space-separated names. Normal login sends the unchanged x-flint-cli-bootstrap-scopes; login with extra permissions sends the desired baseline and additions. No scopes are implicitly added. The browser may approve a subset per context; token scope reports the approved set. Unknown scopes return HTTP 400 invalid_scope. Selected scopes are checked against the selected merchant and environment before approval.

post.description: First-party public client flint-cli. Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and flat OAuth JSON without a Flint envelope. No client secret or HTTP Basic authentication. Requests are not replayed through idempotency caching. Flint session control extension. Starts device consent bound to the current session and user without consuming the refresh token. Without scope_mode, approval replaces consent; denial or expiry leaves consent unchanged. Redeem using the device_code grant to rotate the latest family token. Set scope_mode=additive and context_id to request additional space-separated scope names for one existing context. Merchant and environment are derived from that context; conflicting hints return invalid_context. Approval unions only browser-approved additions with that context's existing scopes and preserves all other contexts. No implicit bootstrap scopes are added. Unsupported or environment-disallowed scopes return HTTP 400 invalid_scope; browser denial returns access_denied when polling. Partial approval succeeds and scope in the token response is authoritative. Legacy single-context sessions must start a new contexts-mode authorization.

post.description: Exchanges an authorization code or refresh token for an installation-scoped bearer token. This endpoint follows OAuth token endpoint conventions: it accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests as well as JSON and returns OAuth token error objects for token exchange failures instead of the normal Flint error envelope. Request rate limits return HTTP 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After and Flint-Rate-Limited-Reason. Device-code token polling returns HTTP 400 slow_down for both early polls and request rate limits. The public client flint-cli also supports the RFC 8628 device_code grant and rotating refresh tokens using form requests. Pending device requests return authorization_pending; early polling returns slow_down and increases the required interval by five seconds; denial returns access_denied; expired or consumed codes return expired_token. Access tokens last 15 minutes. CLI sessions expire after 30 days idle or 90 days total. Reusing a rotated refresh token revokes its family, including when the previous response was lost. A fresh browser login is then required. With session_mode=contexts at authorization, tokens include oauth_session_id and context_id. Refresh requires an explicitly authorized context_id; invalid_context and context_access_denied do not consume the refresh token. Each access token is limited to one context. Ordinary rotation preserves other unexpired access tokens; removing consent immediately invalidates affected tokens. Refresh scope may request a subset of the selected grant or context scopes. Only the issued access token is narrowed; consent and other tokens are unchanged. A later refresh without scope restores the full consented scopes. Legacy sessions retain their original response shape.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update to mutable order fields such as customer_id, notes, metadata, tax, the delivery destination, and the requested tip. A request containing only metadata, internal_note, buyer_note, or external_reference_id, with optional expected_version, can update open, closed, paid, and invoice-locked orders without changing totals. Other merchant edits keep hosted and embedded checkout sessions open unless an edit closes or completes the order, which ends the session with order_mutated. Edits can also end invoice, return-resolution, and subscription-plan sessions with order_mutated. A session already past expires_at ends with expired before the edit is applied. These annotation updates are blocked while any order payment attempt remains non-terminal, including an authorization awaiting capture, or checkout payment work is still resolving. Requests combining annotations with other fields use the financial mutation rules for the entire request. Send requested_tip: null to clear the current requested tip. A merchant can correct a paid subscription signup or renewal destination before shipment by sending delivery_destination and the current order version as expected_version. The committed delivery methods must remain eligible, and shipping and tax totals must stay unchanged. ORDER_DELIVERY_DESTINATION_REPRICE_REQUIRED returns the reason and computed shipping and tax amounts when the correction would change the paid totals.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's receipt email carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in, and lets the buyer have the receipt sent again to the order's email. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the order. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it returns ACCESS_LINK_MERCHANT_HOSTED, and for an order without a customer, ACCESS_LINK_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an Idempotency-Key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with X-Request-Id before sending a new request.

get.description: Returns a read-only, human-readable history log for an order. Use it to render timelines and debug what happened, not as a source of truth, ledger, or webhook replacement. Read the owning resource for authoritative state: the order for balances and status, the payment for payment state, the refund for refund outcomes, and the checkout session for checkout state. Do not sum balance_delta_money to compute an order balance. Informational rows such as payment_failed, refund_failed, and checkout_session_expired have a zero balance delta. The default order is newest first. Use sort_direction=asc for chronological timeline rendering. A typical chronological log might show created, payment_failed, payment, refund, then refund_failed; each row gives one reference to click through for the authoritative resource.

post.description: Starts or resumes a payment attempt on the order. Set action to pay to charge the full outstanding balance, confirm_payment_intents to confirm order-owned payment intents, setup to save a newly collected token on a zero-balance order, or resume to continue an attempt after a pending client action. Each action accepts only its own fields. Only confirm_payment_intents accepts completion_behavior. A pay action without payment_source is valid only when the outstanding balance is zero. To continue a resumable attempt, send action: resume with order_payment_attempt_id and a new Idempotency-Key. An exact retry of the original request with its Idempotency-Key returns the stored response if the request completed, or recovers the same attempt if it was interrupted. Payment intents with manual capture return an active authorization instead of settling immediately. A replay preserves the original HTTP status and domain result. Client authority in payment_attempt.pending_actions is available only within 24 hours of the original request and while the matching current payment attempt has status requires_action. Otherwise pending_actions is empty. Read GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/payment-attempts/{order_payment_attempt_id} for the attempt's current state.

post.description: Queues a receipt for a paid order, including gift card payments and settled payments. Send email to choose a recipient, or omit it to use the order's email. Requires Flint-managed receipt delivery. Sending is limited to once every five minutes per order and normalized recipient. Checkout credentials can send only to the address on file. If no address is on file, checkout credentials can send to at most three distinct addresses over the order's lifetime. Receipts sent for this order through this route count toward this limit, including failed deliveries and receipts sent with a secret API key. Merchant callers can choose any address.

parameters.description: Filter by whether the merchant must capture the payment or respond to a dispute. A dispute requires action when its status is needs_response or inquiry_needs_response, evidence responses are allowed, and its deadline is absent or has not passed. Omit to include both groups.
parameters.name: action_required

parameters.description: Filter by payment intent status.
parameters.name: status

x-enum-descriptions: Waiting for the buyer's payment details. Either nothing has been attempted yet, or the last attempt was declined, failed, or blocked and last_payment_error says why. Confirm again with a new credential.

Payment details are attached, but confirmation hasn't finished. Flint usually confirms in the same request that attaches them, so this status is brief unless that confirmation was interrupted. Resume the order's payment attempt, or call confirm with an empty body for a standalone payment intent. No webhook is sent for this status.

The buyer must finish a step, such as 3D Secure authentication or a redirect, before the payment can continue. current_payment_action describes the step. Afterward, call confirm with an empty body, or resume the order's payment attempt.

Submitted, with the outcome not known yet. ACH debit payments stay here until the bank settles them, which takes a few business days. Card payments pass through briefly. A processing payment intent can't be canceled or updated.
A manual-capture hold is in place and no money has been collected. Capture up to capturable_money, or cancel, before authorization_expires_at.
Canceled before any money was collected, by you or by Flint, for example when an invoice is voided. Final. cancellation_reason says why when Flint knows it. A canceled hold is in released_money.
The payment is collected, and captured_money is the amount. Final.

A manual-capture hold reached authorization_expires_at without a capture, and the funds went back to the buyer. Final. cancellation_reason is authorization_expired, and the payment_intent.canceled event reports it.

x-enum-descriptions: No dispute is recorded for this payment.
The issuer asked for information before any chargeback. Respond by evidence_due_at.
You responded to the inquiry and the issuer is reviewing it.
The inquiry closed without becoming a chargeback. Final.
A chargeback is open and needs your response by evidence_due_at.
Evidence was submitted and the bank is deciding.
Decided against you, or a bank return that could not be contested. Final.
Resolved before it became a chargeback. Final.
Flint received a dispute state it does not recognize yet. Not final. Treat the dispute as open, do not assume an outcome, and read it again later. A response session still opens.

patch.description: Applies a sparse update while status is requires_payment_method, requires_confirmation, requires_action, or requires_capture. In processing, succeeded, canceled, or expired it returns 409 PAYMENT_INTENT_CANNOT_BE_UPDATED, with the status in error.details[].current_status. amount_money can change only while status is requires_payment_method and before the first confirmation attempt; after that, create a new payment intent. customer_id can change only while status is requires_payment_method, and receipt_email only while it is requires_payment_method or requires_confirmation. Send null to clear tip_money, external_reference_id, receipt_email, or all metadata; amount_money and customer_id cannot be cleared. This route doesn't attach a payment source: send the buyer's credential to the confirm route.

post.description: Confirms a standalone payment intent. For the first confirmation, send exactly one of stripe.confirmation_token, payment_source_token, or payment_method_id; without one, it returns FIELD_REQUIRED. After the buyer completes current_payment_action, call this route again with no body or {} to continue the same payment attempt. Flint confirms again only if the processor still requires it, and otherwise returns the current payment intent. Unverified fee fields are omitted. current_payment_action is null when no buyer action is needed. It can also be null while status is requires_action if Flint cannot produce the action yet; retrieve the payment intent again. Order-owned payment intents reject this route and must be confirmed through POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/pay.

parameters.description: Page size, default 20, max 100.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Cursor returned by the previous list response.
parameters.name: page_token

parameters.description: Filter by status. Repeat the parameter or send comma-separated values to match any of several. Omitted, the list leaves out archived rows; name archived to include them.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Filter by whether a promotion can apply now or why it cannot. available matches promotions that can apply now; the other values match unavailable_reason. Repeat the parameter or pass comma-separated values to match several. This filter is ANDed with status, available, and unavailable_reason. Archived promotions still require status=archived.
parameters.name: availability

parameters.description: true lists promotions that can apply now. false lists the others; archived ones only when status names archived.
parameters.name: available

parameters.description: Filter by why a promotion cannot apply now. not_yet_started lists scheduled promotions with a future schedule.starts_at; expired lists ended promotions with schedule.ends_at at or before the current time. Inactive and archived lifecycle states take precedence over schedule, followed by a future start, an ended schedule, exhausted usage, and no active codes. Values within this filter are ORed; status and available are ANDed. Archived promotions still require status=archived.
parameters.name: unavailable_reason

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.
parameters.name: external_reference_id

parameters.description: Search across promotion ID, external reference ID, name, display name, description, and promotion codes. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as ord_01.

post.description: Create or reuse a hosted or embedded checkout session for the buyer's balance on a replacement order linked to this return resolution. Returns 200 when reusing an existing session and 201 when creating one. Omit surface to use hosted. The same surface reuses the open session; changing surface replaces an idle session and is refused while a payment is in progress. Use redirects to set where the buyer goes after paying or canceling. The return_url field is an alias for redirects.success_redirect_url and must be an address of the merchant's customer account. A reused session takes a new success destination only until a payment starts, then keeps its existing destination.

post.description: Creates the link Flint's email about a Return carries, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the Return and its order in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in. Withdrawing the Return needs the buyer to sign in. It works for 30 days or 10 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the Return. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it returns ACCESS_LINK_MERCHANT_HOSTED, and for a Return whose order has no customer, ACCESS_LINK_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an Idempotency-Key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with X-Request-Id before sending a new request.

post.description: Record decisions, receipts, inspections, dispositions, and resolutions for an existing requested or open Return in one request. Refunds, payments, replacement orders, and inventory updates complete asynchronously. expected_version is optional and checked only when sent. If the Return has changed since that version, the request fails with RETURN_VERSION_CONFLICT. When an automatic refund can no longer run through the original payment's provider, the request fails with 409 ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED; send automatic_resolution_type as null to resolve manually, or choose no_monetary_action. Requires Idempotency-Key and all three scopes: commerce.returns.write, commerce.returns.operations.write, and commerce.returns.resolutions.write.

parameters.description: Filter by the system that supplies billing dates.
parameters.name: billing_schedule_owner

parameters.description: Filter external schedules by whether they need another billing date.
parameters.name: awaiting_billing_schedule

parameters.description: When true, returns subscriptions scheduled to cancel at the end of the current period that are not yet canceled. When false, returns every other subscription.
parameters.name: cancel_at_period_end

parameters.description: Filter by Flint customer ID.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Filter by the subscription's selected delivery method.
parameters.name: delivery_method_id

parameters.description: Filter by the reason of the current delivery_hold. Does not match upcoming delivery issues.

parameters.description: Filter by Flint subscription offer ID.
parameters.name: subscription_offer_id

parameters.description: Filter by Flint subscription plan ID.
parameters.name: subscription_plan_id

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on the caller-owned external reference ID.

parameters.description: Search across subscription ID, external reference ID, customer, and plan. Text fields match any part of the value, and %, _ and \ are ordinary characters, not wildcards. IDs match from the start and need the type prefix, such as ord_01.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to created_at; ties are broken by subscription_id.
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.
parameters.name: sort_direction

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on created_at.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on updated_at.
parameters.name: updated_before

parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_after

parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on next_billing_at.
parameters.name: next_billing_before

parameters.description: True matches subscriptions with a delivery hold, an upcoming delivery hold, an inventory wait, or a delivery-action-required pause, plus past_due or incomplete subscriptions and active subscriptions whose billing date passed more than 24 hours ago without a renewal. False is the exact complement. Other filters still apply.

parameters.description: Supported expansions: customer, subscription_plan. Each expansion resolves with one batched lookup per page. post.description: Creates a link like the ones in Flint's subscription email, to put in buyer email or messages you send yourself. It opens the subscription in your Flint-hosted customer account without a sign-in. Changing it, such as pausing or canceling, needs the buyer to sign in. It works for 14 days or 5 opens, whichever comes first; after that the buyer signs in to see the subscription. The url is a bearer credential. Flint returns it only in this response and in a retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so send it only to the buyer and keep it out of logs. A call with a new key creates another link; earlier links keep working until they expire. When customer_account.mode is merchant_hosted it returns ACCESS_LINK_MERCHANT_HOSTED. Send no request body or an empty object ({}). Idempotency is scoped to the merchant, credential, environment, and this resource's route. A replay returns the original link without extending its lifetime or replenishing its opens. Without an Idempotency-Key, each call creates a new link and has no replay result. If Flint cannot retain a result after minting, contact support with X-Request-Id before sending a new request.

patch.description: Sets the next billing date, clears an external schedule while it awaits a date, or transfers schedule ownership. Moving a Flint-owned next_billing_at sets billing_anchor_day to its UTC day unless you send an explicit anchor. Transferring an external schedule to Flint with a next billing date follows the same rule. An unchanged date and owner preserve the anchor. The response carries the updated subscription. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

post.description: Pauses a subscription immediately, optionally for at least one billing cycle. A pause with a duration resumes automatically at scheduled_resume_at. Repeating the stored pause length returns the paused subscription; a different length returns SUBSCRIPTION_ALREADY_PAUSED and requires resuming first. A buyer's pause follows the store's customer_account.buyer_capabilities. Send expected_version to reject a concurrent change.

post.description: Charges the next renewal now, ships it when the subscription has delivery, and moves the next billing date forward by one interval. Available while the subscription is active on a Flint-owned billing schedule (billing_schedule_owner is flint), is not set to cancel at the end of its period, is not in a trial, and has no delivery hold or renewal in progress. The subscription's payment method must be active and allow off-session charges. Requires Idempotency-Key; retry with the same key to recover the same attempt. Returns the subscription, renewal order, and payment attempt with status 200, including when the payment is declined. Inspect payment_attempt.last_payment_error for a failed payment.

x-enum-descriptions: The merchant's available or pending balance changed.
A new balance transaction (charge, refund, dispute, payout, fee, merchant billing collection, or adjustment) was recorded.

A bundle's own fields, images, categories, modifier set or components changed. Copied category names and handles, component variant summaries and delivery readiness send no bundle events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A category was deleted. It can no longer be retrieved.
A category was updated. Assigned product and bundle counts and targeting_reference_count send no category events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A hosted checkout session was closed before payment completed.
A hosted checkout session finished and its payment succeeded.

A checkout session was invalidated because its order closed or was paid elsewhere, an invoice, return-resolution, or subscription-plan change ended it, or a replacement session superseded it. Other order edits keep hosted and embedded sessions open and do not send this event.
A draft credit note was created.
A draft credit note was updated.
A credit note amount was allocated to its invoice.
A credit note allocation was reversed.
A checkout or customer account custom domain changed status.
A customer deletion request completed and the customer was anonymized.
A buyer requested deletion of their customer account data.
A customer deletion request was rejected.
A delivery location set was activated.
A delivery location set was archived.
A delivery location set was created.
A delivery location set was deactivated.
A delivery location set configuration changed.
A delivery rate callback was activated.
A delivery rate callback was archived.
A delivery rate callback was created.
A delivery rate callback was deactivated.
A delivery rate callback configuration changed.
An emergency delivery dependency revocation was created with a safe estimated impact.
A delivery selection became the order's committed fulfillment economics.
First observation of a dispute, in any status.
The inquiry closed without becoming a chargeback.
The dispute status first became lost.
The status entered needs_response or inquiry_needs_response and a response is allowed. This includes inquiry escalation.
The dispute status first became prevented.
Another change to the public dispute representation, including a move to other. Sent only when no condition event applies.
The dispute status first became won.
A merchant environment was granted to a partner app install.
A merchant environment grant was revoked from a partner app install.
An early fraud warning was reported for a payment.
An early fraud warning changed actionability or dispute linkage.
A materialized order fulfillment completed all non-canceled obligated quantity.
A committed fulfillment execution leg materialized as an order fulfillment.
A fulfillment moved between pending, completed, and canceled.
A materialized order fulfillment changed execution state or detail.
A fulfillment event was recorded from a carrier, pickup flow, appointment system, or other fulfillment source.
A gift card was issued. The masked resource includes its posted, reserved and available value.
A gift card balance, reservation, lifecycle, credential or descriptive association changed.
A gift card funding lot was recorded with face value and consideration provenance.
A gift card funding lot's remaining value or risk restriction changed.
A gift card recipient notification was created. The snapshot includes its recipient, status and version.
A gift card recipient notification's delivery status changed. Retrieve the notification for current delivery history.
An exact gift card redemption was reserved or captured.
A gift card redemption was captured, released, expired or refunded.
An immutable gift card financial movement was posted. Corrections create new transactions.
An inventory count was applied and its variances were committed to inventory.
An inventory level has more protected claims than sellable physical stock.
Stock was received into Inventory directly or through a typed Return disposition.
An inventory claim requires a safe merchant action before commerce can continue.
A held or committed inventory claim became insufficiently protected.
An inventory reservation has no active held or committed quantity.
Held inventory quantity became committed order inventory.
An inventory reservation was created with exact location assignments.
A merchant-owned inventory hold reached its deadline.
Held or committed inventory quantity was released.
An inventory transfer reached a terminal state.
Inventory in transit was recorded as lost.
Inventory was received at a transfer's destination.
Inventory in transit was returned to its origin.
An invoice collection block was resolved and the invoice can be collected again.
Invoice collection was blocked because a prerequisite such as inventory changed.
Credit note allocations closed an invoice with no remaining balance.
An invoice email could not be delivered.
A scheduled invoice could not be issued and remains a draft.
An invoice was issued and became open for collection.
A late fee was added to an invoice balance.
An invoice reached a configured late fee date.
The unpaid remainder of an invoice late fee was waived.
A manual (offline) payment was recorded against an invoice.
A previously recorded manual payment was reversed.
An invoice's outstanding balance was written off as uncollectible.
An invoice passed its payment due date with an outstanding balance.
An invoice was paid in full. Sent for online, gift card, and manual payments.
An invoice received a partial payment. Sent for online, gift card, and manual payments.
Part of an invoice's payment was refunded.
An invoice's payment was fully refunded.
An invoice reminder is ready to send.
An invoice was sent to the customer.
An invoice draft or scheduled send time was updated.
An invoice was voided and can no longer be paid.
An invoice payment attempt was canceled.
An invoice payment attempt entered processing.
A merchant's payment, payout, or onboarding readiness was observed in live or sandbox mode.
The amount the merchant owes Flint or owns as account credit changed.
Flint issued a merchant billing invoice.
A merchant billing invoice changed status.
A modifier group's own fields or modifiers changed. Owned collections are included in this object. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A modifier set's own fields, groups or inline modifiers changed. Owned collections are included in this object. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
An order was closed. A paid order closes when it completes, and an unpaid one closes when its checkout expires or its invoice is marked uncollectible. Check payment_status.
An order has an inventory failure that requires operator action.
An order inventory exception was resolved.
An order became fully paid, including by a manual payment on its invoice. Use order.payment_captured for each captured online payment.
An order first became partially paid, including by a manual payment on its invoice. Use order.payment_captured for each captured online payment.
An authorization on an order was canceled.
An authorization on an order expired before capture.
A payment on an order was authorized and is awaiting capture.
An authorized payment on an order was captured.
An order received a full or partial refund.
A partner app install was created.
A partner app install's granted permissions changed.
A partner app install was revoked.
A payment intent fulfillment hold was activated or released.
A payment was submitted and is awaiting its final outcome.
The payment requires a customer action such as 3D Secure authentication.
The payment was authorized and is awaiting capture.
A payment link changed, including being activated or deactivated. Sales through the link don't send this event.
A saved payment method was removed.
A payment method was saved to a customer.
A payout to the merchant's bank was canceled.
A payout to the merchant's bank was created.
A payout failed and funds were returned to the balance.
A payout arrived at the merchant's bank.
A payout destination was removed. It stays readable by ID with status archived.
A payout destination (bank account) was added.
The merchant's payout schedule or settings changed.
A product was archived. Its variants were archived with it and send no events of their own.
A product was created. Each variant it created sends product_variant.created.

A product's own fields, options, images, categories or modifier set changed. Variant changes send product_variant events instead, although they also change the product's rollups and version. Rollups (default_variant, price_range, active_variant_count, variant_count, available_for_sale and delivery_configuration_status) and copied category names and handles send no product events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.
A variant was archived on its own. Archiving its product sends only product.archived.

A product variant was updated. Copied selected option names and values, available_for_sale, effective_images and delivery readiness send no variant events. The object is read when the event is prepared and can include later changes.

get.description: Streams canonical merchant webhook events created after the connection opens or after the supplied event ID. SSE event IDs are resumable webhook event IDs. Control records include ready, gap, withheld, and disconnect. Gap records indicate cursor_unavailable or payload_expired; withheld records hide payloads the caller cannot read. Backpressure emits disconnect with reason backpressure and resume_cursor identifying the last sent event, so clients can reconnect without losing events.

releases.overview: Balance transactions report fees as positive charges that match the payment's `processing_fee_money`, name their timestamp `occurred_at`, and identify the related resource by its own ID field. Tax categories split into `line_item_tax_category` for items and `charge_tax_category` for charges, so the field name tells you which set of values applies.

changes.summary: Balance transaction fee charges are positive and fee credits are negative.
changes.action: Read a positive `fee_money` as a fee charged and a negative one as a fee returned. `net_money` is unchanged.

changes.summary: Balance transaction relationships use resource-specific IDs.
Balance transactions use occurred_at for the transaction timestamp.
Tax categories use line_item_tax_category for items and charge_tax_category for charges.
changes.action: Replace `tax_category` with `line_item_tax_category` on product variants, modifiers, bundles, and line item taxes, and with `charge_tax_category` on delivery methods and charge taxes.
